title: Hoboing toward California and put off the train at Amarillo
summary: He and a friend hobo toward California, are thrown off near Amarillo, and he fails an audition for his sister at a dance.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So, like I was saying, I went to Oklahoma City and I
McGhee (11/16) - 8

got to find out what was happening, and I got discouraged there. I figured I'd go to California to see what was happening. So I got on a train, and me and another cat named Hill, Frank Hill I think his name was, we got on a...hoboed on a train to go to California. And the train stopped right outside of Amarillo [SOUNDS LIKE 'Camarillo.'] And the brakeman saw us on the train and put us off, you know. He said, "You ain't got no business being on this," you know, so forth and so on. Anyway, we...
How old were you then?
Oh, I was just about... Still young.
Still young.
Yeah. Maybe fourteen or fifteen, somewhere around there.
Little did you realize what Camarillo was going to mean later on with Bird.

Yeah. Well, at that time I didn't know they had a Camarillo! I was thinking about going to California. I just wanted to be in California, you know, because I heard that it was pretty good out there, and they had a lot of music going on out there, and they were making pictures and so forth.
Now, Hill was a musician also?
Andrew, no, he was no Hill... Uh, Hill, he
McGhee (11/16) - 9
wasn't a musician, no. But he wanted to go to California, so I figured here's a buddy to run with. But they put us off the train anyway, right outside of Amarillo, Texas.
Oh, Amarillo.
Yeah.
Oh, I thought you had said Camarillo in California.

No-no. Amarillo, Texas. And luckily, we caught a train coming back into Amarillo, so I got that. And I found out my sister was there in town! So I went and found her, and she fed us both and she had my clothes cleaned and pressed, and so forth, so I'd look halfway decent. And I told her I could play the trumpet. And by that time..> They were having a dance that same night anyway. So she said, 'Good. I can take you down there and if you can play some, the guy will let you play, and I can hear what you sound like.'
So I went down and tried to play. I didn't know my ass from a hole in the ground, frankly speaking, to let you know where I was at! Anyway...
You got to start some place.
Everybody has to start some way, so I figured I might as well do that.
So in the meantime, after that was over... Actually, I made a big flop there, because she said, 'No-o, I don't

think so." She didn't think I had played so good, which I didn't, because I didn't know what I was doing anyway. I was just trying, you know! And I got a job around there trying to shine shoes and shit, but I never liked that -- I just couldn't see shining no goddamn shoes.
